title: Prune old snapshots (keep last N)
description:
snapshots, health_snapshot_files, and health_snapshot_components grow unboundedly — no DELETE anywhere in the codebase. Observed: sutra's own DB has 503 snapshots and 6,396 health_snapshot_files rows; redox-kernel accumulated 205 empty snapshots. Each parse appends 1 snapshot + ~1 row per file + 1 per component (insert_snapshot_atomic, src/db/mod.rs:1447).

Fix: after inserting a snapshot, delete snapshots (and their file/component score rows) beyond the most recent N (suggest 50, possibly configurable). Check sutra_trend's window requirements before picking N.

acceptance_criteria.text: snapshot count stays bounded at N after repeated parses
score rows deleted with their parent snapshot
sutra_trend still works over its expected window

implementation_plan:
1. Add `Db::prune_snapshots(&self, keep: usize) -> Result<usize>` — deletes children then parents beyond the newest `keep` snapshots.
2. Call prune(30) after successful COMMIT in `insert_snapshot_atomic`.
3. Add test in `tests/db-test.rs` verifying retention count and child cleanup.
N = 30, no config knob.
execution_record: Implemented as planned. N=30. prune_snapshots deletes children (health_snapshot_files, health_snapshot_components) then parent snapshots beyond the newest 30, called after each insert_snapshot_atomic COMMIT. Made prune_snapshots pub so the test can exercise it with a small N (keep=3) independently of the hardcoded constant. No config knob added.
